sections.label: Section A - Reading Skills, General Knowledge & Logical Reasoning

questions.stem:
"Stop taking this medicine and tell your doctor immediately if you notice any of the following rare side effects: swelling of the face, lips or throat, difficulty breathing, or a severe skin rash with blistering. Common side effects include nausea and headache. Uncommon side effects include dizziness and sleep disturbance. The frequency of certain other effects cannot be determined based on available data."

From the informational leaflet for a prescription antihistamine

Which of the following statements is the correct interpretation of the information contained in this excerpt?
options: A patient who develops a blistering skin rash while taking this medicine should stop taking it and contact a doctor immediately.
Nausea is a rarer side effect of this medicine than a severe skin rash.
Difficulty breathing is a common side effect of this medicine.
Every patient who takes this medicine experiences at least one side effect.
Sleep disturbance is a reason to stop the medicine immediately.
questions.exp: The leaflet places a severe blistering rash in the group of rare effects for which the instruction is to stop the medicine and tell a doctor immediately, so the matching interpretation is the one about the blistering rash. Nausea is listed as common, so calling it rarer than the rash reverses the frequency ranking, and difficulty breathing belongs to the rare, urgent group rather than the common one. No statement in the leaflet supports the claim that every patient has side effects, and immediate stopping is reserved for the rare effects, not for sleep disturbance.
questions.topic: Reading · medicine leaflet (frequency bands and urgent effects)

questions.stem:
"Street trees and small parks measurably cool dense neighbourhoods in summer. In a survey of ten Mediterranean cities, streets whose canopy covered more than 30% of the view from the pavement were on average 2.1 °C cooler on summer afternoons than otherwise similar streets with sparse canopy. The difference was largest in districts with low buildings and narrow streets, where shaded surfaces trap less heat. Cooling depended on species and on irrigation: unwatered young trees grew too slowly in dry summers to shade anything. City planners quoted in the report treat canopy as one instrument among several, alongside reflective roofs and lighter pavements."

From a newspaper report on urban climate research

Indicate which of the following statements is not correct:
options: Streets with more than 30% canopy cover were, on average, cooler than similar streets with sparse canopy in the survey.
How well trees cool a street can depend on the species and on whether the trees are watered.
Tree planting has been shown by the report to be a complete solution to summer heat in Mediterranean cities.
In districts with low buildings and narrow streets, the cooling difference associated with canopy was largest.
The report presents canopy as one of several instruments available to city planners.
questions.exp: The report describes canopy as one instrument among several, alongside reflective roofs and lighter pavements, so the statement claiming tree planting is a complete solution contradicts the passage and is the incorrect one. The other four statements restate the survey's comparisons, the role of species and irrigation, and the district effect faithfully.

questions.stem:
"In this country the ruler causes money to be made from the inner bark of mulberry trees, pressed into sheets like paper and cut into round pieces of different values. With this money everything can be bought throughout the whole empire. Refusing it is punishable, and every year the ruler causes all the mulberry bark that can be gathered to be bought up. It costs him almost nothing, yet with it he buys the goods of merchants from every land, who must accept it in exchange."

Adapted from The Travels of Marco Polo (13th century)

What does the passage describe?
options: Gold coins stamped with the ruler's seal
Paper money issued by a ruler
Letters of credit drawn on banks
Barter between merchants and the ruler
questions.exp: The money is described as sheets pressed from mulberry bark, cut into pieces of different values and imposed as legal tender across the empire, which identifies it as state-issued paper money. Gold coins and letters of credit are different instruments, and barter contradicts the requirement that merchants accept the money in exchange.

questions.stem:
"Bacteria in the large intestine ferment fibres that human digestive enzymes cannot break down. The fermentation releases short-chain fatty acids, which are absorbed and used by the cells of the intestinal wall as an energy source. Some of these acids also enter the bloodstream and influence the activity of immune cells. The composition of the bacterial population differs between people and shifts with diet over weeks."

From a popular science book on the human body

Only one of the following statements is coherent with the excerpt:
options: Gut bacteria can convert dietary fibre into substances that the body absorbs and uses.
Human digestive enzymes release short-chain fatty acids from fibre in the small intestine.
The bacterial population of the intestine is fixed at birth and does not change with diet.
Short-chain fatty acids act only inside the intestinal lumen and never enter the blood.
Immune cell activity is independent of the products of gut bacteria.
questions.exp: The passage states that bacteria ferment fibre into short-chain fatty acids which are absorbed and used, some of them reaching the bloodstream and influencing immune cells, so the first statement is the coherent one. The claim that human enzymes do this in the small intestine contradicts the opening sentence, the fixed-population claim contradicts the shift with diet, and the last two claims reverse what is said about the bloodstream and immune cells.

questions.stem:
Consider this statement: Every chemist working in this laboratory speaks German.
Which of the following statements is deducible from the given statement?
options: Everyone in the laboratory who speaks German is a chemist.
Someone working in the laboratory who does not speak German is not one of its chemists.
Nobody in the laboratory speaks German.
Some chemists working in the laboratory do not speak German.
German is spoken in the laboratory only by chemists.
questions.exp: If every chemist in the laboratory speaks German, then anyone in the laboratory who lacks German cannot belong to that group of chemists, which is the contrapositive. The claim that everyone speaking German is a chemist is the converse, which does not follow, and the remaining options contradict or go beyond the given statement.
questions.topic: Logic · deduction from a universal statement

questions.stem:
From the given statements:
If the vaccine shipment arrives on Monday, then the clinic starts the vaccination campaign on Tuesday.
The campaign did not start on Tuesday.
Which conclusion can be deduced?
options: The vaccine shipment arrived on Monday.
The campaign will start on Wednesday.
The vaccine shipment did not arrive on Monday.
questions.exp: By modus tollens, if arriving on Monday would force a Tuesday start and there was no Tuesday start, the shipment cannot have arrived on Monday. Saying the shipment was lost goes beyond the premises, since a delay or a holiday closure would also be consistent with no Tuesday start.

questions.stem: Five runners, Ada, Beppe, Chiara, Dario and Elena, finished a race with no tied places. Dario finished before Chiara, Chiara finished before Ada, Ada finished before Beppe, and Beppe finished before Elena. Which of the following statements can be deduced?
questions.exp: The constraints chain into the single order Dario, Chiara, Ada, Beppe, Elena, so Elena is behind every runner who precedes Beppe, including Chiara. The other four statements each reverse one of the given relations.

questions.stem: Three friends, Nadia, Omar and Paolo, each drove home in a different car, one red, one blue and one white. Nadia drove neither the red nor the blue car, and Omar did not drive the blue car. Which of the following statements is true?
questions.exp: Nadia driving neither red nor blue forces her into the white car, and since Omar did not drive blue and white is taken, Omar drove red, leaving blue for Paolo. Every other option contradicts this unique assignment.

questions.stem: A watch gains 3 minutes every hour. It is set to the correct time at 8:00 am. When the true time is 10:00 am, the watch shows:
questions.exp: In the two hours since 8:00 am the watch has gained 2 × 3 = 6 minutes, so at a true time of 10:00 am it reads 10:06 am. The 10:03 option counts only one hour of gain, 9:57 am treats the watch as losing time, and 10:09 am triples the gain.

questions.stem: The immediate benefit that lactic fermentation provides to a muscle cell working without enough oxygen is that it:
options: produces a large amount of ATP by oxidising lactate completely.
converts lactate into glycogen for storage.
restores NAD⁺ so that glycolysis can continue producing ATP.
releases the energy of reduced FAD for ATP synthesis.
transports pyruvate into the mitochondrial matrix.
questions.exp: Fermentation reduces pyruvate to lactate, and this step reoxidises the cell's NADH to NAD⁺, allowing glycolysis to continue making its small ATP yield; without regenerated NAD⁺, glycolysis stalls. Lactate is not oxidised for ATP inside the muscle cell, and the other options describe steps of aerobic respiration that fermentation does not perform.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements about glycolysis is correct?
options: It takes place in the cytosol and produces a net gain of 2 ATP per glucose molecule.
It takes place inside the mitochondrial matrix and produces a net gain of 4 ATP per glucose molecule.
It requires molecular oxygen in its first step.
It reduces FAD to FADH₂ during the oxidation of glucose 6-phosphate.
It converts glucose directly into acetyl-CoA without forming pyruvate.
questions.exp: Glycolysis is the cytosolic splitting of glucose into two pyruvate molecules with a net yield of 2 ATP and 2 NADH. Oxygen is not required at any glycolytic step, FAD is not involved because FADH₂ is produced later in the Krebs cycle, and pyruvate, not acetyl-CoA, is the product of glycolysis.

questions.stem: In a eukaryotic cell supplied with oxygen, the largest share of the ATP produced from one glucose molecule comes from:
options: the conversion of pyruvate to acetyl-CoA.
questions.exp: Of the roughly 30 ATP obtained from one glucose molecule, about 26 arise when the reduced coenzymes produced by the earlier stages are oxidised through the electron transport chain, that is by oxidative phosphorylation. Glycolysis and the Krebs cycle contribute only 2 ATP each by direct transfer of phosphate, the link reaction contributes none, and fermentation adds nothing beyond the yield of glycolysis.

questions.stem: ATP synthase of the inner mitochondrial membrane produces ATP using the energy released by:
options: electrons jumping directly onto oxygen molecules.
protons flowing down their gradient through the enzyme.
direct transfer of a phosphate group from NADH to ADP.
diffusion of glucose across the membrane.
questions.exp: In chemiosmosis, the electron transport chain pumps protons into the intermembrane space, and the stored gradient drives protons back through ATP synthase, which couples this flow to the phosphorylation of ADP. Oxygen serves only as the final electron acceptor at the end of the chain, and no phosphate group is handed over directly from NADH.

questions.stem: In the mitochondrial respiratory chain, which carrier transfers electrons from complex I to complex III?
questions.exp: Ubiquinone is the lipid-soluble mobile carrier that accepts electrons from complex I, and also from complex II, and delivers them to complex III. Cytochrome c performs the analogous transfer but between complexes III and IV, NADH donates electrons to complex I rather than shuttling between complexes, and oxygen only receives electrons at complex IV.

questions.stem: In a tissue that is metabolising actively and releasing much CO₂, haemoglobin releases oxygen more readily because:
options: H⁺ and CO₂ bind to haemoglobin and lower its affinity for oxygen.
the rising pH shifts haemoglobin into a high-affinity state.
CO₂ competes with oxygen for the iron atom of the heme group.
oxygen bound to one heme group prevents oxygen from binding to the others.
the red blood cells take up bicarbonate and expel all their oxygen.
questions.exp: This is the Bohr effect: protons and CO₂ bind to haemoglobin at sites other than the heme iron, stabilising the low-affinity state and so promoting oxygen unloading exactly where metabolism is most active. CO₂ lowers the blood pH rather than raising it, and the cooperative binding of oxygen works in the opposite direction to the one described.

questions.stem: In skeletal muscle, the calcium ions released during contraction bind to troponin. The effect of this binding is to:
options: detach the myosin heads from actin permanently.
provide the energy for the power stroke.
move tropomyosin away from the myosin-binding sites on actin.
hydrolyse the ATP attached to the myosin heads.
questions.exp: Calcium binding to troponin shifts the attached tropomyosin and exposes the myosin-binding sites on actin, allowing cross-bridge cycling to begin. ATP hydrolysis on the myosin head provides the energy for the power stroke, and the filaments slide past each other without changing length.

questions.stem: Cardiac muscle cells are joined end to end by intercalated discs containing gap junctions. The main function of these junctions is to:
options: anchor the cells firmly to the heart's tendons.
allow rapid electrical coupling between adjacent cells.
synthesise the collagen fibres of the heart skeleton.
increase the surface area available for gas exchange.
store oxygen within the muscle cells.
questions.exp: The gap junctions of the intercalated discs let ions flow directly from cell to cell, so the excitation begun at the pacemaker spreads across the whole chamber and makes it contract as a single unit. Anchoring and collagen roles belong to connective structures, and oxygen is stored by myoglobin, not by junctions.

questions.stem: During contraction of a sarcomere, which region remains unchanged in length?
options: The I band together with the H zone
questions.exp: The A band corresponds to the full length of the myosin filaments, which do not shorten, so it stays constant while the sarcomere contracts. The I band, which contains actin only, and the H zone, where myosin has no overlapping actin, both become narrower as the filaments slide.

questions.stem: The effect of a competitive inhibitor on an enzyme-catalysed reaction can be overcome effectively by:
options: increasing the concentration of the substrate.
increasing the concentration of a cofactor of the enzyme.
raising the pH to the enzyme's optimum value.
questions.exp: A competitive inhibitor occupies the active site and competes with the substrate, so a sufficiently high substrate concentration can outcompete it and restore the reaction's maximum rate. Cofactors, temperature and pH do not displace an active-site competitor, and adding a second inhibitor can only reduce the rate further.

questions.stem: A small organic non-protein molecule that must be bound to an enzyme for the enzyme to show its activity is called:
questions.exp: Coenzymes are organic cofactors, such as NAD⁺ or FAD, that must associate with the protein part for activity. The apoenzyme is the inactive protein alone and the holoenzyme is the active complex of protein plus cofactor, a zymogen is an inactive enzyme precursor, and a substrate analogue is a mimic that blocks the active site rather than activating the enzyme.

questions.stem: Which digestive enzyme acts in the stomach and has an optimum pH of about 2?
questions.exp: The hydrochloric acid of the stomach gives pepsin its strongly acidic optimum around pH 2, at which it hydrolyses proteins into peptides. Amylase, trypsin, maltase and lipase all work at near-neutral to mildly alkaline pH in the mouth, pancreas or small intestine.

questions.stem: In the liver, the toxic ammonia produced by the breakdown of amino acids is converted mainly into:
questions.exp: Mammals detoxify ammonia in the liver through the urea cycle, and the urea produced passes to the blood for excretion by the kidneys. Uric acid is the nitrogen waste of birds and reptiles, creatinine comes from phosphocreatine breakdown in muscle, and ammonia is not routed into carbon dioxide or glucose by this pathway.

questions.stem: If the secretion of antidiuretic hormone (ADH) stops, the most direct consequence for the kidneys is that the person produces:
options: a small volume of highly concentrated urine.
urine with an abnormally high sodium concentration and no other change.
a large volume of dilute urine.
questions.exp: ADH makes the collecting duct permeable to water by driving the insertion of aquaporin channels; without it, water is no longer reabsorbed there, so the urine stays dilute and its volume is large. Glucose in the urine signals high blood glucose instead, and urine formation continues without ADH, it is only its volume and concentration that change.
questions.topic: Bio · osmoregulation (ADH and the collecting duct)

questions.stem: The cells that resorb bone matrix by secreting acid and digestive enzymes are:
questions.exp: Osteoclasts break down bone by sealing off a region of matrix, acidifying it and releasing enzymes, which releases calcium into the blood. Osteoblasts build new matrix, osteocytes are the mature cells maintaining bone in lacunae, and chondroblasts and fibroblasts form cartilage and connective tissue.

questions.stem: Which hormone raises the concentration of glucose in the blood by stimulating glycogen breakdown in the liver?
questions.exp: Glucagon, secreted by the alpha cells of the pancreas when blood glucose falls, activates glycogen phosphorylase in the liver and so raises blood glucose. Insulin has the opposite effect, and aldosterone and melatonin regulate salt balance and circadian rhythms rather than blood glucose.

questions.stem: The bond that joins two glucose units within glycogen is:
questions.exp: Monosaccharides are linked in glycogen, starch and cellulose by glycosidic bonds, formed by condensation reactions between hydroxyl groups of adjacent sugars. Peptide bonds join amino acids, ester bonds join glycerol to fatty acids, and phosphodiester bonds join nucleotides in nucleic acids.

questions.stem: A cell is treated with ouabain, a poison that blocks the sodium-potassium pump. The most direct consequence is that the cell gradually:
options: reverses the direction of the Na⁺/K⁺ gradient across its membrane.
loses the Na⁺/K⁺ concentration gradient across its membrane.
becomes freely permeable to all ions.
increases its rate of ATP production.
starts pumping potassium out and sodium in.
questions.exp: The pump maintains the gradients by exporting 3 Na⁺ and importing 2 K⁺ for each ATP hydrolysed, so blocking it allows the gradients to decay through ion leakage. The blocked pump neither reverses direction nor makes the membrane non-specific, and removing an ATP consumer reduces, rather than increases, ATP use.

questions.stem: A digestive enzyme secreted by a pancreatic cell reaches the plasma membrane by passing through which sequence of structures?
options: Free ribosome, then nucleus, then plasma membrane.
Rough ER, Golgi apparatus, secretory vesicle, plasma membrane.
Golgi apparatus, rough ER, lysosome, plasma membrane.
Smooth ER, Golgi apparatus, nucleus, plasma membrane.
Rough ER, lysosome, Golgi apparatus, plasma membrane.
questions.exp: Secreted proteins begin on ribosomes attached to the rough ER, pass into its lumen, travel in vesicles to the Golgi apparatus for modification and sorting, and finally leave in secretory vesicles that fuse with the plasma membrane. The routes through the nucleus or the lysosomes do not occur for secretory cargo.

questions.stem: Lysosomal enzymes are synthesised on the rough ER and are then sorted, tagged and packaged for delivery to the lysosomes by:
questions.exp: After synthesis on the rough ER, lysosomal enzymes move to the Golgi apparatus, where they receive a targeting tag and are packed into vesicles that fuse with lysosomes. The smooth ER handles lipids and detoxification, and the nucleolus assembles ribosomal subunits.

questions.stem: A triglyceride molecule consists of:
options: glycerol, two fatty acids and one phosphate group.
three amino acids joined to glycerol.
one glucose unit joined to three fatty acids.
questions.exp: A triglyceride is one glycerol molecule esterified to three fatty acid chains, the form in which fat is stored in adipose tissue. The molecule bearing a phosphate group instead of one fatty acid is a phospholipid, and amino acids and glucose are not components of triglycerides.

questions.stem: The ability to taste a certain bitter compound is controlled by a dominant allele T. A man who is a heterozygous taster (Tt) and a woman who cannot taste the compound (tt) have a child. The probability that the child cannot taste the compound is:
questions.exp: The cross Tt × tt gives half Tt tasters and half tt non-tasters, so the probability of a child who cannot taste is 1/2. The fractions 1/4 and 3/4 come from a Tt × Tt cross, which this is not.

questions.stem: During quiet inhalation, which of the following occurs?
options: The diaphragm relaxes and rises back into the thorax.
The internal intercostal muscles contract strongly.
The diaphragm contracts and the thoracic volume increases.
The pressure inside the alveoli rises above atmospheric pressure.
The rib cage is pulled inward.
questions.exp: Inhalation is active: the contracting diaphragm flattens and the external intercostal muscles raise the ribs, enlarging the thoracic cavity so that alveolar pressure falls below atmospheric pressure and air flows in. A relaxing, rising diaphragm and alveolar pressure above atmospheric both describe exhalation.

questions.stem: A 0.001 mol/dm³ solution of a monoprotic weak acid has a pH of 4.0. The acid dissociation constant Ka of this acid is approximately:
questions.exp: A pH of 4.0 means [H⁺] = 1.0 × 10⁻⁴ mol/dm³, and for a weak acid Ka = [H⁺]²/C = (1.0 × 10⁻⁴)²/0.001 = 1.0 × 10⁻⁵. The value 1.0 × 10⁻⁴ wrongly equates Ka with [H⁺] itself, and 1.0 × 10⁻⁷ comes from multiplying [H⁺] by C instead of squaring and dividing.
questions.topic: Chem · weak acid pH (deriving Ka from pH)

questions.stem: An aqueous solution of ammonium chloride, NH₄Cl, the salt of a strong acid and a weak base, is:
options: neutral, because it is a salt and salts do not affect pH.
acidic, because NH₄⁺ donates a proton to water.
basic, because Cl⁻ is a strong base.
basic, because NH₄⁺ releases hydroxide ions.
impossible to classify without knowing the concentration.
questions.exp: NH₄⁺ is the conjugate acid of the weak base ammonia and releases a proton to water, generating H₃O⁺, while Cl⁻, the conjugate base of a strong acid, is a spectator, so the solution is acidic. The concentration changes how acidic the solution is but not the direction of the effect.

questions.stem: A solid substance does not conduct electricity at all, but the same substance in the molten state conducts well. The substance is most likely:
questions.exp: In an ionic solid the ions are fixed in the lattice and cannot carry charge, but melting frees them to move, which is exactly the behaviour described. Copper conducts as a solid because of its delocalised electrons, while sulfur, silicon dioxide and glucose neither conduct as solids nor as melts.

questions.stem: Which of the following bonds is the most polar? (Pauling electronegativities: H = 2.20, C = 2.55, N = 3.04, O = 3.44, Cl = 3.16)
questions.exp: Polarity grows with the electronegativity difference between the bonded atoms, and oxygen differs most from carbon among the partners listed, so C–O is the most polar bond. Chlorine and nitrogen follow, C–H is only weakly polar, and C–C joins identical atoms and is non-polar.

questions.stem: What is the average oxidation number of sulfur in sodium thiosulfate, Na₂S₂O₃?
questions.exp: With sodium at +1 (two atoms) and oxygen at −2 (three atoms), the two sulfur atoms must together contribute +2, giving an average of +2 per sulfur. The value +6 belongs to sulfur in sulfate and −2 to sulfide, neither of which matches this ion.

questions.stem: In the reaction 2Mg + CO₂ → 2MgO + C, which species is oxidised?
options: Carbon, because its oxidation number falls from +4 to 0.
CO₂, because it loses oxygen atoms.
Both magnesium and carbon are oxidised.
Magnesium, because its oxidation number rises from 0 to +2.
questions.exp: Oxidation means an increase in oxidation number, and magnesium goes from 0 in the element to +2 in MgO, losing two electrons that reduce the carbon of CO₂. Carbon falling from +4 to 0 is reduction, and oxygen switching partners is not by itself a redox change.

questions.stem: Which of the following compounds is a ketone?
questions.exp: Propanone, CH₃COCH₃, carries its carbonyl group on a carbon within the chain, which is the defining feature of a ketone. Propanal and methanal are aldehydes with the carbonyl at the end of the chain, propan-1-ol is an alcohol and propanoic acid is a carboxylic acid.

questions.stem: Which of the following pairs contains only monosaccharides?
questions.exp: Glucose, fructose and galactose are single sugar units, whereas sucrose, maltose and lactose are disaccharides built from two such units, and starch and cellulose are polysaccharides. Only the glucose and fructose pair consists of two monosaccharides.
questions.topic: Chem · carbohydrates (mono- vs di- vs polysaccharides)

questions.stem: What amount of oxygen, in moles, is required for the complete combustion of 0.5 mol of propane? (C₃H₈ + 5O₂ → 3CO₂ + 4H₂O)
questions.exp: The balanced equation uses 5 mol of O₂ per mol of propane, so 0.5 mol requires 2.5 mol of oxygen. The values 1.5 and 2.0 mol are the amounts of CO₂ and of H₂O formed, not of oxygen consumed.

questions.stem: What mass of water is produced when 4.0 g of methane burns completely in excess oxygen? (CH₄ + 2O₂ → CO₂ + 2H₂O; molar masses: CH₄ = 16 g/mol, H₂O = 18 g/mol)
questions.exp: 4.0 g of methane is 0.25 mol, and each mole of methane yields 2 mol of water, giving 0.5 mol, that is 9.0 g. The 4.5 g option forgets the factor of 2 in the equation and the larger values lose track of the mole amount of methane.

questions.stem: Going from left to right across a period of the periodic table, the first ionisation energy of the elements generally:
options: increases, because nuclear charge rises while the outer electrons enter the same shell.
decreases, because the atoms become heavier.
remains constant, because the shell number does not change.
increases, because the atomic radius increases.
decreases, because the outer electron lies further from the nucleus.
questions.exp: Across a period, protons are added to the nucleus while the outer electrons occupy the same shell, so attraction on the outer electron grows and more energy is needed to remove it. Atomic radius in fact decreases across a period, so the claims based on growing radius are wrong.

questions.stem: The maximum number of electrons that the 3p sublevel can hold is:
questions.exp: A p sublevel contains three orbitals, each holding two electrons of opposite spin, giving 6 in total. The value 2 is the capacity of a single orbital, 8 is the total for the whole second shell and 10 is the capacity of a d sublevel.

questions.stem: The industrial synthesis of ammonia is exothermic: N₂(g) + 3H₂(g) ⇌ 2NH₃(g), ΔH < 0. Which set of conditions gives the highest equilibrium yield of NH₃?
options: Any temperature, provided a catalyst is used
questions.exp: The forward reaction converts 4 mol of gas into 2, so high pressure pushes the equilibrium towards ammonia, and because the reaction is exothermic, low temperature favours the products. A catalyst speeds both directions equally and changes the rate of reaching equilibrium, never its position.
questions.topic: Chem · equilibrium (Le Chatelier on ammonia synthesis)

questions.stem: Adding a catalyst to a reversible reaction already at equilibrium:
options: raises the activation energy of the forward reaction only.
lowers the activation energies of forward and reverse reactions and does not shift the position of equilibrium.
shifts the equilibrium position towards the products.
increases the enthalpy change of the reaction.
increases the concentrations of the reactants.
questions.exp: A catalyst offers an alternative path of lower activation energy for both directions, so forward and reverse rates rise equally and the equilibrium composition stays the same. Since the enthalpy change depends only on initial and final states, it is untouched, and no concentration is altered.

questions.stem: The compound CuSO₄ is correctly named:
questions.exp: The sulfate ion SO₄²⁻ carries a double charge, so the single copper ion in the formula must be Cu²⁺, giving copper(II) sulfate. Sulfite is SO₃²⁻ with one oxygen fewer, sulfide is the simple S²⁻ ion, and copper(I) would require the formula Cu₂SO₄.

questions.stem: The set of real solutions of the inequality x² + 2x + 5 ≤ 0 is:
options: the set of all real numbers.
questions.exp: The discriminant is 2² − 4 × 1 × 5 = −16, which is negative, so the upward-opening parabola never touches or crosses the x-axis and the expression is always positive, leaving no real solution. The value x = −1 is only the vertex position and does not satisfy the inequality.

questions.stem: Solve the inequality 5x − 3 < 2x + 9.
questions.exp: Moving the x terms to one side gives 3x < 12, and dividing by the positive number 3 keeps the sense of the inequality, so x < 4. No sign flip occurs because the divisor is positive, and the x < 12 option forgets to divide.

questions.stem: The equation x² − 5x + k = 0 has one root equal to 2. The value of k is:
questions.exp: Substituting x = 2 gives 4 − 10 + k = 0, so k = 6; the other root is then 3, since the two roots sum to 5. The value 4 copies the square of the given root and 10 copies the middle coefficient.
questions.topic: Maths · quadratic equations (using a known root)

questions.stem: If A = {1, 2, 3, 4} and B = {3, 4, 5, 6}, how many elements does A ∪ B contain?
questions.exp: The union collects every element of both sets, with the shared elements 3 and 4 counted once, giving {1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6}, that is 6 elements. The value 8 forgets the overlap and the value 4 counts only one set.

questions.stem: The product (2x − 3)(x + 5) is equal to:
questions.exp: Multiplying term by term gives 2x² + 10x − 3x − 15, and combining the middle terms gives 2x² + 7x − 15. The 13x option adds 10x and 3x instead of subtracting, and the sign errors on the constant or the leading coefficient produce the other wrong forms.

questions.stem: A rectangle's length is 3 cm greater than its width, and its perimeter is 26 cm. Its width is:
questions.exp: Writing w for the width, the perimeter is 2(w + w + 3) = 26, so 2w + 3 = 13 and w = 5, with length 8. The 8 cm option reports the length rather than the width.

questions.stem: If sin θ = 0.6 and θ is an acute angle, then cos θ is:
questions.exp: From sin²θ + cos²θ = 1, cos²θ = 1 − 0.36 = 0.64, and because θ is acute the cosine is positive, cos θ = 0.8. The value 0.36 is sin²θ itself and 0.4 is double the true shortfall.

questions.stem: A car travels along a straight motorway at a constant 90 km/h, following a truck that travels at a constant 72 km/h and is 2.0 km ahead. After 5 minutes, which statement is correct?
options: The car has overtaken the truck.
The car has not yet caught the truck.
The car has drawn exactly level with the truck.
The car will never catch the truck.
The car needs more than a further hour to catch the truck.
questions.exp: The gap closes at the relative speed of 90 − 72 = 18 km/h, so in 5 minutes, one twelfth of an hour, the car gains 18/12 = 1.5 km and still trails by 0.5 km. Closing the full 2.0 km takes 2.0/18 of an hour, about 6.7 minutes in total, so the car is close but not yet level.

questions.stem: A circuit contains two resistors of 6 Ω each connected in parallel, and this pair is connected in series with a single 3 Ω resistor. The equivalent resistance of the whole network is:
questions.exp: The two equal 6 Ω resistors in parallel give 6/2 = 3 Ω, and adding the series resistor gives 3 + 3 = 6 Ω. The 15 Ω option treats the parallel pair as a series pair, giving 12 + 3, and the 9 Ω option uses a single 6 Ω in series with 3 Ω.

questions.stem: A wire of uniform material is replaced by a new wire that is twice as long and has half the cross-sectional area. Compared with the original wire, the resistance of the new wire is:
questions.exp: Resistance is proportional to length and inversely proportional to area, R = ρL/A, so doubling L multiplies R by 2 and halving A multiplies it by a further 2, giving four times the original resistance. The unchanged and doubling options each account for only one of the two changes.
questions.topic: Physics · resistance of a wire (R = ρL/A)

questions.stem: At what height above the Earth's surface is the acceleration due to gravity equal to one quarter of its value at the surface? (The Earth's radius is R.)
questions.exp: Gravitational acceleration falls as the inverse square of the distance from the Earth's centre, so quartering g requires doubling that distance from R to 2R, which means a height of one radius, R, above the surface. The answers R/2 and 2R come from inverting or misplacing the square.

questions.stem: A car of mass 1.5 × 10³ kg accelerates along a level road at 2.0 m/s² against a constant frictional force of 500 N. The force the engine must exert is:
questions.exp: Newton's second law gives the net force as ma = 1500 × 2.0 = 3000 N, and the engine must also cancel the 500 N of friction, so it exerts 3500 N. The 3000 N option ignores friction, and 2500 N subtracts it from the net force instead of adding it.
questions.topic: Physics · dynamics (Newton's second law with friction)

questions.stem: A swimming pool is 4 m deep. Taking the density of water as 1000 kg/m³ and g = 10 m/s², the gauge pressure of the water at the bottom of the pool is:
questions.exp: Hydrostatic gauge pressure is ρgh = 1000 × 10 × 4 = 40000 Pa. The 4000 Pa option drops one power of ten and 400000 Pa adds one; note that atmospheric pressure is excluded because the question asks for gauge pressure.
